answer: Admission here is paid in judged labour: a vertex votes only after delivering jetty, tasks that randomly drawn judges score as useful, capped at one per epoch per vertex. The atlas links each vertex to the keys and payout wallets behind it, so siblings collide there and the k-th vertex of one operator owes k² jetty. An honest vertex waits one epoch for 1 jetty, but 1,000 clones owe about 333 million jetty, the last alone a million epochs of real work. It breaks if judges collude or links in the atlas can be cheaply hidden.
